the thermal-expansion of highly-oriented pyrolytic graphene layers is anomalous at the magic-angle and that the anomalous behavior is related to the presence of superconductivity-like hystereses in the magnetization.

the anomalous T-dependent variation of the c-axis of HOPG samples is due to an intrinsic property of graphite which involves the presence of superconductivity-like hystereses and the saturation of the thermal expansion coefficient.
the anomalous variation of graphite’s c-axis in the low-temperature regime (12-298 K) is related to the misfit-rotations and the superconducting-like behavior.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reported saturation-effect is not due to the presence of superconductivity in the samples.
the anomalous T-dependence of the c-axis of the graphite sample is related to the presence of the magic-rotational-angle and that it is not due to the presence of a bulk superconductor.
the anomalous c-axis variation and superconducting-like behavior is a direct consequence of a strong interaction between graphene layers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the reported saturation-effect in the c-axis is due to the interplay of the magnetic and structural properties of graphite and it is a signature of the presence of a superconducting-like state.

the reported saturation-effect in the c-axis and the presence of superconductivity-like hystereses could be due to the interplay of the graphene-layer misfit-rotation and the graphene-layers stacking in the graphite structure.

the anomalous T-dependent variation of the c-axis and the presence of superconductivity-like effects are related to a complex interplay of the interlayer interaction and the interlayer-phonon-structure of the graphite sample, which is not yet fully understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the anomalous behavior in the c-axis is not a simple effect of the graphite-layer misorientation but it is rather due to the interlayer interactions which are strongly affected by the misorientation angle.
the reported anomalous T-dependence is a consequence of the high degree of graphene layer orientation and misfit-rotation angle of the sample.
a novel T-X-ray-diffraction approach can be used to study the thermal-expansion of graphite and other layered materials with a high degree of graphene-orientation and misorientation-angle.
